CausalChain: BNCT delivers high-LET radiation -> induces localized tumor cell death and immunogenic cell death (ICD) -> releases DAMPs and neoantigens -> dendritic cells uptake tumor antigens but may be suboptimally activated -> administration of a TLR agonist boosts dendritic cell maturation -> enhanced presentation of tumor antigens to T cells -> systemic anti-tumor immune response including abscopal effects
Hypothesis: Combining BNCT with a post-treatment regimen of toll-like receptor agonists will enhance dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation, thereby amplifying tumor-specific T-cell responses and inducing both local and abscopal anti-tumor effects in cancers that are traditionally resistant to systemic immunotherapy.
Abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) has emerged as a highly selective modality for targeting malignant cells by delivering localized high linear energy transfer radiation, yet treatment responses remain limited by local recurrence and systemic disease spread. Recent findings suggest that BNCT-induced tumor cell death may release damage‐associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and neoantigens that potentially prime an anti‐tumor immune response. Here, we propose a novel hypothesis that the post-BNCT tumor microenvironment can be modulated using toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists to enhance dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation. This approach may convert the immunologically ‘cold’ tumor milieu into a systemically immunogenic “hot” environment, increase tumor-specific T-cell infiltration, and promote robust abscopal effects. Our hypothesis offers an integrative treatment paradigm that combines the precision of BNCT with immune system adjuvants, thereby potentially amplifying both local and systemic anti-tumor responses.
